cells: Magma cools below surface; slow cooling produces large crystals.
Lava cools rapidly on surface; small crystals.

blocks.content: Igneous rocks, often called primary rocks, are formed through the cooling, crystallization, and solidification of magma or lava.

items: Granite (Acidic Intrusive) and Basalt (Basic Extrusive) are major components of continental and oceanic crusts respectively.
Deccan Traps in India are composed of flood basaltic extrusive igneous rocks.
Questions frequently distinguish between Plutonic (Granite, Gabbro) and Volcanic (Basalt, Obsidian) igneous rocks based on grain size and mineral composition.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Igneous rocks are formed by the cooling and solidification of molten magma or lava.
Based on mode of occurrence, they are divided into Plutonic (deep-seated), Hypabyssal (intermediate depth), and Extrusive/Volcanic (surface).
Chemical classification categorizes igneous rocks into Acidic (silica-rich) and Basic/Ultrabasic (iron and magnesium-rich).
Cooling speed dictates texture: slow subterranean cooling creates coarse-grained (phaneritic) rocks, while rapid surface cooling forms fine-grained (aphanitic) rocks.
